title: Evaluating Deadlocks with Inverted and Concessive Past Conditions

sections.content: You know *si hubiera* + past participle (with *habría* in the result) from B1 Unit 35, *aun cuando* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 8, and both *de haber* + participle and *si*-less *Hubiera / Hubiese* + participle (plus *aun cuando* with the pluperfect subjunctive) from B2 Unit 10. In post-negotiation assessments, mediators combine these three elevated conditional patterns to evaluate turning points: what would have happened without a timely intervention (*De no haber intercedido...*), what a flexible stance would have achieved earlier (*Hubieran transigido a tiempo...*), and why an intransigent demand would have failed even under favourable conditions (*Aun cuando hubieran modificado el pliego...*).

sections.title: High-Register Counterfactuals in Negotiation Analysis
rows: *De haber / De no haber* + participle, conditional perfect
De no haber intercedido la mediadora, el diálogo se habría roto. (Had the mediator not interceded, the dialogue would have broken down.)
Hubieran transigido antes, habrían firmado la tregua en mayo. (Had they compromised earlier, they would have signed the truce in May.)
Aun cuando hubieran aceptado el pliego, habría faltado financiación. (Even if they had accepted the list of demands, funding would have been lacking.)

items.spanish: De haber mantenido una postura intransigente, no habrían logrado la tregua.
items.english: Had they maintained an intransigent stance, they would not have achieved the truce.

items.spanish: De no haber limado asperezas en privado, la sesión habría fracasado.
items.english: Had they not smoothed over rough edges in private, the session would have failed.

items.spanish: Hubiese intercedido el comité a tiempo, se habría apaciguado el ánimo.
items.english: Had the committee interceded in time, tempers would have been calmed.

items.spanish: Aun cuando hubieran retirado aquel pliego, la contraparte habría exigido garantías.
items.english: Even if they had withdrawn that list of demands, the counterpart would have demanded guarantees.

sections.content: After preposition *de*, only the perfect infinitive follows: *De haber transigido*, never *De hubiera transigido*. Conversely, when you open directly with a finite verb without *si*, only the pluperfect subjunctive (*Hubiera / Hubiese transigido*) is valid, never the conditional *Habría*.
